plan.title: Run the Overdeck Anywhere release acceptance criteria on integrated main
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

metadata.sizeJustification: This is a release acceptance run, not a feature: it necessarily touches one test hook (src/dashboard), the CI workflow, two test helpers and one test, the smoke script, per-AC evidence files under .pan/uat/pan-4774/, and three docs. The issue asks for one run with one closing comment covering AC-1..AC-15, so splitting into sibling issues would break the single status report; most of the surface is evidence files, not code.

narratives.Problem: Every Overdeck Anywhere work item merged, but no one has run the release acceptance criteria AC-1..AC-15 (.pan/drafts/pan-2350.md) end to end on integrated main; each issue verified only its own slice.
narratives.Proposal: Add one CI-run Node test for AC-1 (two dist dashboards with separate OVERDECK_HOMEs, a scripted fake claude, a one-env-var adopt hook so the pull applies into a distinct checkout) that also checks AC-14 and the local half of AC-2; extend the two-machine smoke with needs-docker and --hold; run every local criterion with the smoke and isolated Playwright; run the infrastructure criteria on real Fly VMs, the hosted directory and a peer test dashboard, destroying every VM; record one evidence file per criterion under .pan/uat/pan-4774/; write docs/ANYWHERE-RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md; post a closing comment giving every AC passed, failed (with issue) or approximated (with what was not covered).
narratives.NonGoals:
- No user-facing feature work; the only src/ change is the D-2 test-only env hook, and failures beyond the D-4 fix threshold become new issues
- No phone push test; AC-7 is reported as approximated (desktop Chrome, no phone), never passed
- No new route exposing channel byte counters; AC-14 is measured at the proxy
- No edit of the operator's home config.yaml, projects.yaml or ~/.ssh/config, and no stop/restart of the home dashboard
- No copying of account.json between machines; each machine signs in with its own device flow
- No committed Docker images or Fly app configs for AC-6/AC-10; their text lives in the checklist
- The full two-machine smoke is not added to CI; only the AC-1 test runs in CI
- No skipIf/.only in the new test; no loosening of the 15 s or byte-budget bounds to make it pass
- No Fly machine or volume left running after its item ends

autoDecisions.summary: The AC-1 CI test is a vitest .slow.test.ts run by its own step in the test-e2e job, with tmux installed in that step.
autoDecisions.rationale: vitest.config.ts excludes *.slow.test.ts unless VITEST_INCLUDE_SLOW=1, shards use 5 s default timeouts, CI has no tmux, and the test-skip gate forbids skipIf; a dedicated step makes it blocking through test-all-passed.

autoDecisions.summary: Add the test-only env var OVERDECK_TEST_ADOPT_SKIP_SAVED_CWD to resolveTarget so the single-host pull applies the WIP bundle into A's own checkout.
autoDecisions.rationale: On one host A adopts into B's checkout and nothing is applied; the transfer store's key is in memory only, and a mount namespace needs sudo. Precedent: OVERDECK_TEST_FORCE_CPU_SATURATED in machine-load.ts.

autoDecisions.summary: Measure AC-14 at the byte-counting proxy in front of B rather than exposing ChannelSocket counters.
autoDecisions.rationale: Proxy bytes include channel framing, so they bound the channel counters from above; no new route is needed.

autoDecisions.summary: AC-2 local half uses the proxy capture; the relay half uses tcpdump as root inside the AC-3 Fly VM.
autoDecisions.rationale: sudo needs a password on this host and tcpdump has no capabilities; the issue allows the channel frame dump when tcpdump is unavailable.

autoDecisions.summary: AC-10 runs on a throwaway systemd image with a volume at /home and the packed integrated-main tarball, with an approximated fallback if systemd cannot run as PID 1 on Fly.
autoDecisions.rationale: The pan-workspace image has no systemd, pan connect needs a systemd user manager with lingering, and the Fly rootfs resets on restart; the issue tests integrated main, not the published package.

autoDecisions.summary: AC-4's three machines are the home dashboard plus two Fly VMs.
autoDecisions.rationale: A peer dashboard on the same host is not a separate machine; the issue requires Fly among the three.

autoDecisions.summary: AC-7 and AC-11 run against peer test dashboards; AC-11's sealed-storage half is evidenced by directory-smoke.mjs step inbox under Miniflare.
autoDecisions.rationale: Stopping or subscribing the home dashboard would change operator state; production Durable Object storage cannot be inspected.

autoDecisions.summary: Directory-registering items (AC-3 VM, AC-10 VPS, AC-11 peer) run serially and each forgets its machine.
autoDecisions.rationale: The account's plan tier is unknown and a free account allows 3 machines.

autoDecisions.summary: Fix-or-file threshold: fix here when at most two source files, under 60 added lines, one subsystem, with a failing-first unit test; otherwise file an issue with step, command, output and commit.
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue says fix small local failures and file larger ones; a numeric threshold removes the judgment call.

autoDecisions.summary: AC-5 and AC-4 use a temporary throwaway project pan4774-anywhere-smoke (a fresh clone of an unregistered public eltmon repo), removed after AC-4.
autoDecisions.rationale: Every registered home project is a primary checkout, and pulling into a clean target checks out the snapshot's branch there (wip-apply.ts), which would drift a primary checkout.

autoDecisions.summary: Evidence files live in .pan/uat/pan-4774/, one per run item.
autoDecisions.rationale: Precedent .pan/uat/pan-4743/ and .pan/notes/pan-4320-live-verification.md; one file per item avoids shared-file edges between independent runs.

Add the AC-1 two-machine slow test under tests/integration/anywhere

narrative.Action: PRD WI-4. Write tests/integration/anywhere/two-machine-ac1.slow.test.ts with beforeAll(startPair, 120 s), afterAll(stop) and the seven ordered tests from the PRD with their explicit timeouts: links both ways (both 'online' within 15 s of the link command), lists each other's conversations within 15 s (seeded rows on both sides; assert @<B>/<name> on A and @<A>/<name> on B), opens within the NFR-9 budget (proxy bytes from B > 0 and <= 1114112 for a >2 MiB transcript), remote-controls a live fake-claude conversation on B (delivery method set to 'tmux'; B's input log contains 'ping-4774'; A's /messages contains 'fake-reply:ping-4774' within 30 s; match substrings), pulls it with uncommitted changes (A's own clone at <A>/live with the same origin https://github.com/smoke/repo.git registered in A's projects.yaml; `pan conv pull @<B>/<name> --stop-turn --json` state 'done'; the new row's cwd is <A>/live and <A>/live/uncommitted.txt has the written text), the old owner refuses new turns (409 conversation-released on B directly and through A), nothing crossed in plaintext (capture[0] === 0x00 and no 'HTTP/1.1'). No skipIf, no .only, no source-file reads. If the 15 s conversation-list bound fails on integrated main, that is an AC-1 finding: apply the D-4 fix-or-file rule instead of loosening the bound.

Link a Fly VM over a direct route, then through TURN with UDP blocked (AC-3, AC-2 relay)

narrative.Action: PRD WI-14, D-5, D-8. Create the VM with `fly machine run` (pan-workspace image, shared-cpu-1x) and start `pan serve` on it by hand; do NOT use `pan machines add-fly`, because that links over the Fly public-link route, which outranks a directory route and hides whether rtc:// works. Link it only through the directory. `pan account login` on the VM: send the device code and URL with `pan tell conv-flywheel "<code> <url>"` (Bash sandbox disabled) and wait for approval. Join through the directory (join/approve/accept). With no Tailscale on either side, `pan machines list --json` on home shows a current route starting rtc://. Inside the VM block UDP except DNS (`iptables -A OUTPUT -p udp --dport 53 -j ACCEPT; iptables -A INPUT -p udp --sport 53 -j ACCEPT; iptables -A OUTPUT -p udp -j DROP; iptables -A INPUT -p udp -j DROP`, so connect.overdeck.ai still resolves through Fly's resolver), re-establish the link, and show it runs over the relay (Using relay, bytes used rising). Run `tcpdump -i any -w /tmp/relay.pcap` in the VM while a conversation open crosses the relay with a marker string; `strings /tmp/relay.pcap | grep -c -e <marker> -e 'HTTP/1.1'` must print 0.
